clue.text: Fictional scientist, as read by Charlie after academic period

indicators.note: says the fool's word comes behind the academic period

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
a term is a period of the academic year
a charlie is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A fictional scientist's lines are voiced by someone called Charlie, following a stretch of term time.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is not a name here but British slang for a fool. Professor Quatermass was the scientist hero of 1950s BBC television serials.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor Bernard Quatermass is the invented scientist of the BBC science-fiction serials, so he is an example of a fictional scientist.

clue.text: Part of port and game queen repeatedly avoided

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the harbour a game is played in which the queen is twice dodged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a pastime such as chess, where a queen might be avoided, but it means hunted prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is the wharf where ships tie up, one of the structures making up a harbour.

clue.text: Floored a jerk landing a left

explanation.definitionFit: Being floored by a question means being baffled by it, utterly unsure what to do or say: an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Record whistling sound in retreat of leisure woodland area

explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for a hideaway, but it turns the word 'of' around to give FO. Epping Forest is a large ancient woodland on London's north-east edge, run for public recreation.
explanation.definitionFit: Epping Forest is a large tract of ancient trees in Essex, an example of a woodland area kept for public enjoyment.

clue.text: Folk restricting a water supply have good intentions

explanation.definitionFit: To mean well is an idiom for acting with kindly aims even when the result goes wrong.

clue.text: Labourer could get this site around West Yorkshire's summit

clue.text: Spiritual trip experienced by junkie primarily

explanation.definitionFit: The hajj, also spelt hadj, is the pilgrimage to Mecca, a journey made for religious reasons.

clue.text: Report from mum in courtyard initially missing ring

clue.text: Two private rooms churchman's done up for singer

clue.text: Screenwriter's new picture protected by short warning sign

clue.text: Personal transmitter broadcasting clearer in van

clue.text: Horse leads in race over at Newmarket
